title: Attractive but Flawed Pan
text:
Attractive but Flawed Pan. I love cooking with cast-iron cookware and I have a modest collection of pots and pans. This is my first enameled frying pan, and I will be honest, it is disappointing. It works well enough but the fit and finish is lacking.

This pan is actually quite attractive. It is glazed red on the outside such that it looks like it is weathered and heavily used even though it's brand new. The inside is black; I have seen some enameled pans that are white, and I mention the color more as a data point than anything else.

It has a good weight to it - less weighty than my standard 10.5" cast iron skillet, though it outweighs my carbon steel pan. The handle is a good length and the helper handle makes transport easy.

Where I have difficulty with this pan is in the finish. The lip around the edge of the pan is actually not glazed and is exposed cast iron. This is easy enough to season, though doesn't seem like much thought went into it. My particular pan itself has a defect that can be seen on the top and bottom, though, almost like something flat and mostly round was used to pick up the pan while it was still hot. It does not affect usability but it is visibly obvious. The glaze on the cooking surface, though, is the biggest disappointment. It feels gritty like unseasoned cast iron and it is not as non-stick (even with butter or oil) as it should be as a result.

This pan is useful for cooking when the benefit of using glazed cast iron isn't really needed. An example is in making English muffins or similar goods that do not require oil.

This is an attractive pan and I will get some use out of it, but the fit and finish are lacking. The cost is low, and the quality is on par with the cost.
